expected_claims.claim_text_normalized: YOLO formulates object detection as a single regression problem from raw pixels to bounding box coordinates and class probabilities, using one neural network for the entire task.
The base YOLO model processes images at approximately 45 frames per second on a Titan X GPU, while the Fast YOLO variant reaches around 155 FPS.
Detection is performed by dividing the input image into a fixed grid where each cell predicts a small number of bounding boxes with confidence scores and class probabilities.
YOLO produces more localization errors than two-stage detectors and struggles with small objects appearing in groups.
When evaluated on artwork datasets such as Picasso and People-Art, YOLO generalizes better than detectors trained only on natural images.
Two-stage region-based detectors achieve noticeably higher detection accuracy than YOLO, but at the cost of substantially lower inference throughput.
